title: KKL theorem for balanced functions
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ be a $\pm 1$-valued Boolean function that is balanced, meaning $\E[f] = 0$, and suppose $n \ge 2$. Then there is a coordinate $i \in [n]$ whose influence satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \;\ge\; \frac{\log n}{30\,n}.
\]
replaced:
(Kahn--Kalai--Linial, 1988.) Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ be balanced,
i.e.\ $\E[f] = 0$, with $n \ge 2$. Then some coordinate $i$ has
\[
  \mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \;\ge\; \frac{\log n}{30\,n}.
\]
